- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative and prices are trending down.  
- Lag in correction: model often overshoots early in the forecast horizon, then gradually adjusts — apply downward pressure on later days if sentiment remains negative.  
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen forecasts if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- Overshoot after strong positive sentiment: if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model may overcorrect — reduce forecast peak slightly.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating near-term highs; cap forecast peaks at 1–2 days after sentiment peaks.  
- Negative sentiment amplifies underestimation bias — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment < -0.20.  
- Positive sentiment reduces underestimation bias — allow slight upward adjustment if sentiment > 0.10, but cap at 1.5% above baseline.
